candidate_findings.title: Percent-encoded sensitive query names bypass HTTP log redaction
candidate_findings.trigger: A request supplies a percent-encoded spelling of the access_token or token query key. ASP.NET query consumers use the decoded name, while SanitizeQueryString compares the raw substring before equals.
candidate_findings.impact: The credential-bearing query value can be emitted at Information in both HTTP request and response Path properties. Clean removes controls/length only and does not redact the value. No actual credential or historical log was inspected.
candidate_findings.minimal_recommendation: Parse query names with the same decoding semantics as request consumers and redact the whole sensitive value; prefer an explicit safe query allowlist. Test harmless markers with encoded/case-varied/repeated/malformed keys and capture request+response records.
candidate_findings.dedup: No existing register finding specifically covers this query-name bypass. OPS-015 is a distinct Realtime RPC full-notification-text sink; OPS-003/010 concern Git history scanning, not runtime HTTP logging.

candidate_findings.confidence: CONFIRMED_BUFFER_AND_RESTORATION_DEFECT; streaming effect LIKELY until transport regression
candidate_findings.title: HTTP logging buffers all non-gRPC responses and leaves a disposed replacement stream
candidate_findings.trigger: A non-gRPC response is large, long-lived/streaming, canceled or propagates an exception beyond the logger. Every response body is replaced with a MemoryStream; output is copied only after next completes and the original Body is never reassigned.
candidate_findings.impact: Response buffering has no size cap; downstream flushes target the memory stream. After return/throw Response.Body references the disposed stream, and a copy exception can mask the original failure. CopyToAsync does not observe RequestAborted. SignalR SSE/default transport is a condition-dependent reachable server surface; current frontend explicitly selects WebSockets, so no current-client fallback regression is claimed.
candidate_findings.minimal_recommendation: Log status/content-length without buffering; if byte counting is required, use bounded pass-through instrumentation and always restore Body in a finally block. Add isolated flush/cancellation/exception/large-response regressions and a real SSE transport test before claiming streaming impact.
candidate_findings.dedup: No existing register finding names this logging-response buffering/restoration boundary. DIST-004/005/012 concern authorization, persistence/push and late effects, not this stream wrapper.

candidate_findings.title: Authenticated HTTP response logs can retain UserId=Anonymous with inbound claim mapping

evidence.lines: Authentication Model / Reading the user id from claims

candidate_findings.trigger: A successful request uses a JWT principal whose sub was mapped to ClaimTypes.NameIdentifier by the configured inbound mapping. HttpLoggingMiddleware looks only for raw sub.
candidate_findings.impact: The response log explicitly supplies UserId=Anonymous, and AddPropertyIfAbsent in the correct enterprise UserIdEnricher cannot replace that property. This weakens audit correlation; it is not an authorization bypass. The pre-auth incoming log is legitimately anonymous.
candidate_findings.minimal_recommendation: Use the shared subject resolver or the established sub/NameIdentifier fallback for the response record; cover mapped and unmapped principals with a captured logger.
candidate_findings.dedup: Existing claims guidance documents the convention, but no finding in the current register covers this HTTP audit-property collision.

privacy_observations.observation: Typed BusinessEvents envelopes expose PII/content when serialized, but their constructors were not found in application callers. Do not claim current use from declarations alone.

Actual LoginCommandHandler sends Email/IpAddress, and first-category creation sends category.Name through IBusinessEventLogger Data scope at Information. The active CompactJsonFormatter sink retains structured scope properties. This is data-minimization evidence related to OPS-015, not proof of unauthorized log access or a credential leak.

Historical secret scanning findings do not cover runtime query redaction.
